A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FeRA framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original style-adaptation and DreamBooth experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and generated-image examples, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds a 100-trajectory spectral analysis, reported wall-clock measurements, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: The DoG-based frequency-energy indicator, MLP-softmax expert router, LoRA mixture, and FECL objective remain unchanged in Equations 3–11. The added theoretical discussion and explanation of parameter-budget matching do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five CIVITAI styles and five DreamBooth subject categories. The human study samples existing test-set prompts. Appendix C discusses line art and other non-natural domains but does not document an identifiable additional benchmark evaluation.

E2.justification: Appendix F introduces a LoRA-only comparator selection for the new human-preference comparison. Existing benchmark comparisons retain LoRA, DoRA, AdaLoRA, SaRA, and full tuning; the routing ablation variants also remain unchanged. The added Time-MoE formalization is not a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The theoretical relative per-step runtime comparison in v1 Section 9.3 becomes measured end-to-end latency per generated image in v2 Section 5.5. New protocols include analysis of 100 generation trajectories and a blind, randomized human evaluation using 30 prompts and 20 evaluators. The common training configuration remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a targeted analysis of whether FEI contains instance-specific information beyond timestep, using 100 trajectories and Figure 8. Appendix F adds perceptual validation of style alignment and visual fidelity. The existing router, expert-count, band-count, and FECL ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies matching random seeds for human-study image pairs and displays the population mean and instance-level dispersion across trajectories. It adds no benchmark confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The runtime ranges in v1 were theoretical estimates, not statistical uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Numerous reported values change: Table 1 FeRA SD 3.0/20M Hornify FID changes from 161.94 to 151.94, and SDXL/5M Barbie CLIP changes from 35.86 to 37.86 in v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 6. Most SD 1.5 customization entries are revised. New human-study win rates are 68.5% for style and 62.0% for fidelity. Latency results are replaced under a different measurement protocol.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces a formal comparison of time-dependent and state-dependent routing, a proposition claiming generalization of time-based policies, and two theorems concerning gradient noise and sparsity, with Equations 12–17. These formal statements and arguments have no counterpart in v1; the original SNR and method equations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same scientific scope: frequency-energy analysis, soft expert routing, consistency regularization, and improved diffusion adaptation. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices A–C substantially expand the mechanism and applicability arguments: FEI is interpreted as more than a timestep proxy, routing as closed-loop control and implicit curriculum learning, and frequency awareness as compatible with non-natural image statistics. v1 primarily discusses coarse-to-fine progression and routing continuity.

D1.justification: v2 explains that expert ranks scale inversely with expert count to maintain matched parameter budgets, and specifies the latency measurement boundaries. Its abstract changes code availability from promised to available, although the PDFs cannot verify access. The training-settings table and MLLM judging prompt are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Park et al. (2023, 2024), Lee et al. (2024), Fei et al. (2024), and Yang et al. (2023), while removing Riquelme et al. (2021). These refine diffusion-expert coverage without substantially changing the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: Most core prose is retained. v2 locally revises the introduction and ablation discussion, condenses the conclusion, moves runtime discussion into the main text, and regroups existing supplementary material into Appendices D–E. Author credits, citation style, and a generic impact statement also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML-style layout with running headers and single-column appendices, adds Figures 8, 9, and 14, and relocates the runtime table. Main Figures 4 and 5 shrink from three example rows to two, removing the Barbie and toy-duck rows. Existing tables and supplementary image grids are extensively repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added trajectory analysis, human evaluation, measured latency, and parameter-matching explanation provide useful evidence and clarity. However, Appendix B's vanishing-gradient guarantee does not follow from the unconstrained MLP-softmax router, and Appendix F describes forced choice while reporting unexplained ties. These substantive theoretical and reporting issues leave the net quality benefit of the additions uncertain.
